findings.detail: Fsync transaction and recovery-envelopes then existing keys before install/active rename; old/new retained; injected keys-sync failure cannot reach rename.

Proof now binds both original sources and private DB/WAL to capture hashes, including absent WAL, before and after native; private SHM may be generated. Pre-call and nominal-native-success mutation regressions preserve original bytes and consume key.

reviewed_invariants: Raw-key x-hex pragma agrees with production driver; JNI opens READONLY/NOFOLLOW without CREATE/URI/immutable, rejects plaintext/empty/missing/nonregular before encrypted page reads; no migration or original connection/checkpoint.

Snapshot requires asserted exclusive closed lease, canonical non-symlink paths, stable DB/WAL/SHM/envelope sources and no reset/hot journal; hashes complement a future real lease and are not isolation from arbitrary same-UID mutation.

Native proof checks encrypted schema, supported version, required tables, quick_check and cipher_integrity_check; native and Kotlin candidate buffers are wiped. Local amalgamation confirms cipher_integrity_check errors produce rows and no-row is healthy.

Envelope CAS preserves active until rename, retains exact old/new bytes for ambiguous outcomes, reconciles by exact active bytes rather than phase marker; no alias deletion. directorySynced false remains separate from observed COMMITTED.
V2 codec validates paired canonical aliases and bounded sizes, preserves legacy reader refusal; checksum is corruption detection, not authenticated provenance.
Exact JNI gate permits only two named classes and tests missing/extra old/new/arbitrary class scenarios; no automatic expansion to arbitrary classes.
Source usage search found no production issuer, provider, setup, UI or active storage caller. New native symbol alone is not activation.
limits: No build, JVM, JNI, device or power-loss result is claimed by this review; 23 JVM methods and 4 encrypted Android methods are authored only.
No production closed/exclusive lease issuer; all writer/open/reset/recovery exclusion and final CAS/rename admission still need implementation and runtime proof.

RecoveryEnvelopeTransaction is an internal filesystem primitive, not key-recovery authority; proof-to-candidate-wrap binding, authenticated factor readback and production V2 provider behavior remain absent.
Strict private WAL identity includes absence; if actual read-only SQLite changes private WAL, native acceptance must fail and any accommodation needs explicit review.
Power-loss durability, interrupted real encrypted proof, hostile same-UID races, Keystore authentication, user recovery UI and Fold acceptance remain open.
